evidence.says: Steven W. Sowards is listed at Michigan State University Libraries in 1997.
Steven Sowards is listed as a Library History Round Table officer in 1998–99.

basis: The contemporaneous library affiliation is consistent with the second key, but the sources found do not identify the author of the specific 1998 H-LIS review or link that review to the other key's works. The H-Net review page could not be accessed to check its byline or affiliation.

evidence.says: Cody E. Ferguson reviewed Kathryn Newfont's Blue Ridge Commons for H-Environment in November 2012.
Cody Ferguson completed the dissertation 'This is our land, we have the right to be heard' in 2012.
Cody Ferguson wrote This Is Our Land and was an assistant professor of history at Our Lady of the Lake University.

basis: The review and dissertation share a name and date, but the sources found do not connect the reviewer to the dissertation or book author. Similar subject matter alone does not establish identity.

evidence.says: Christian Keller of Würzburg authored the 2016 report and presented a dissertation project on Hans Blumenberg's ethics at the 2015 conference.
Christian B. Keller earned a Penn State PhD in 2001, has been a history professor since 2011, and wrote Chancellorsville and the Germans.

basis: The report author was undertaking a philosophy dissertation project in Würzburg in 2015; the author of Chancellorsville had completed a different doctorate in 2001 and was a history professor during that period. These are distinct careers and dissertation projects.

evidence.says: George Sandys (2002) is by James Ellison, described as an honorary research fellow at the University of Strathclyde.
The catalogue lists George Sandys (2002) under Ellison, James (1955–).

basis: The book identifies its author with Strathclyde, but no source found connects him to the University of Florida reviewer or to the review. The different affiliations alone do not establish two people.

evidence.says: Robert Wilfred Hannah, BA Yale and MAT Harvard, received a Michigan State history PhD in 1969 for The Origins of Indirect Rule in Northern Nigeria, 1890-1904.
Robert Hannah, author of Greek and Roman Calendars and Time in Antiquity, earned a BA at Otago, studied at Oxford, and joined Otago Classics in 1980.

basis: The thesis author and the books' author have distinct educational and career profiles: the former had a Yale BA and Michigan State history PhD by 1969, while the latter's publisher describes an Otago BA, Oxford study and an Otago classics career. The identification as different people is a strong inference from those profiles rather than an explicit comparison by a source.

evidence.says: Medicine and Duty names editor Marjorie Barron Norris, a Calgary historian who previously wrote about the Calgary Local Council of Women.
The library catalogue lists A Leaven of Ladies by Marjorie Norris, published in 1995.

basis: The publisher connects the two books on the first key, but the sources found do not connect their author to the 1970 dissertation on the second key. The shared name and compatible dates are insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: Fabio López Lázaro earned a Toronto PhD in 1996 and published The Misfortunes of Alonso Ramírez in 2011.
López-Lázaro's 2008 Crime in Early Bourbon Madrid includes an introduction titled ‘The Public’s Vengeance’.
López Lázaro's Toronto dissertation is titled No Crime Safe in its Hiding Place: Crime and Society in Early Modern Spain.

basis: The matching year and distinctive phrase suggest a connection, but the sources do not identify the thesis title on key a or explicitly connect it to the later book. The dissertation title reported by Calgary differs, so the required identity link remains unconfirmed.

evidence.says: Jennifer Ford edited The Hour of Our Nation's Agony, worked at the University of Mississippi from 1998, and earned her history PhD there.
Jennifer Ford completed Landscape and Material Life in Southwestern Pennsylvania, 1798-1838 at Pittsburgh in 2001; her position is listed at Interpretive Solutions.
The 2012 Mississippi faculty catalog lists archivist Jennifer Ford's BA, MA and MLS, without a doctorate.

basis: The Nelson editor's documented Mississippi career and later Mississippi doctorate differ from the Pittsburgh dissertation author's 2001 doctorate and listed position. The 2012 faculty catalog's degree listing further supports that the editor did not hold the 2001 Pittsburgh doctorate.

evidence.says: Jerry J. Frank wrote Making Rocky Mountain National Park (2013) and is identified as a University of Missouri history professor.
Jerry Frank reviewed Michael J. Makley's Saving Lake Tahoe for H-Environment in October 2015.

basis: The review gives no affiliation, and the sources found do not link its reviewer to the author of the book. The shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: The 2009 review of Alltagsbewältigung in der Steiermark names Wolfgang Göderle, Graz, as reviewer; Stefan Benedik Karner is a book editor.
Stefan Benedik's CV lists the 2007 book and the 2012 Cucumbers Fighting Migrations chapter coauthored with W. Göderle.
The University of Graz profile identifies Wolfgang Göderle with ORCID 0000-0002-9417-5316 and lists Administration, Science, and the State.

basis: The reviewed book's editor also coauthored a work on the other key, suggesting a connection. The review names Graz but gives no institutional affiliation, and no source found identifies its reviewer with the ORCID holder or lists works from both keys.

evidence.says: The University of Windsor library lists The revolution in the New York party systems, 1840-1860 under Mark L. Berger.
A 2006 journal list identifies Mark T. Berger as a senior lecturer at the University of New South Wales.

basis: The book is credited to Mark L. Berger, whereas the review key is Mark T. Berger at UNSW. The different middle initials suggest separate people, but the sources do not establish distinct careers or rule out a name variation.

evidence.says: David Alan Rich is the author of The Tsar's Colonels and is described as an independent scholar and researcher at the U.S. Department of Justice.

basis: The book's author is identified, but the sources found do not link him to the 1980 dissertation or establish a distinct career for its author. The shared name alone does not resolve the pair.

evidence.says: Thomas P. Walsh wrote Tin Pan Alley and the Philippines; he holds graduate degrees from the University of Pennsylvania and the University of Hawaii.
Arizona State University's 2015 graduation program names Thomas K. Walsh as the history doctoral graduate who wrote The Public Face of History.

basis: The named authors of the two works have conflicting middle initials, and the book author's documented career and degrees differ from the dissertation record. This supports different people, although the sources do not explicitly compare them.

evidence.says: Indiana University lists Gordon Warren's history dissertation, The Trent Affair: A Study of Anglo-American Public Opinion, 1861-62, for 1968/1969.
The bibliography credits Gordon H. Warren with Fountain of Discontent: The Trent Affair and the Freedom of the Seas (1981).

basis: The sources identify the dissertation and book separately, but do not establish that their authors are the same person or that the book grew out of the dissertation. The shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Cites P. C. Cook, EFTA: The Origins and History of the European Free Trade Association, as a PhD thesis, Ann Arbor, 1969.
Lists Zion City, Illinois: Twentieth Century Utopia by Philip L. Cook, Colorado, August 1965.
Cites Philip Lee Cook's Zion City, Illinois as a 1965 PhD thesis at the University of Colorado.

basis: The keys have distinct doctoral theses credited to P. C. Cook and Philip Lee Cook within a few years of each other. The different initials and closely dated doctorates support two people, although the EFTA citation gives Ann Arbor as the thesis publication place rather than identifying the degree-granting university.

evidence.says: Bootleggers and Borders is by Stephen T. Moore, a history professor at Central Washington University.
Stephen D. Moore wrote the history PhD dissertation Losing Minorca: An Event in English Political History, completed in January 2009.

basis: The two works are attributed to scholars with different middle initials, and the second is a distinct history doctorate. The book author's established Central Washington career and the York dissertation support treating them as different people.

evidence.says: John Wendell Bailey received a Marquette history PhD in 1974 for General Terry and the Decline of the Sioux, 1866-1890.

basis: The supplied AHA records identify two distinct doctoral dissertations: the 1964 constitutionalism thesis and John Wendell Bailey's 1974 Marquette history dissertation. These separate doctorates support treating the keys as different people.

evidence.says: Thomas D. Cockrell wrote the 1989 Mississippi State University PhD dissertation ‘Meadow Woods, 1839-1989: A Mississippi Plantation.’
Thomas D. Cockrell coedited A Mississippi Rebel in the Army of Northern Virginia and is described as a history professor at Northeast Mississippi Community College.

basis: The dissertation and book editor share the full name Thomas D. Cockrell, but the sources found do not link the dissertation to the editor or establish a matching institutional affiliation during the relevant years. The shared name and subject alone are insufficient to merge the keys.

evidence.says: Andrea Hauser, Bremen, reviewed Geerbte Dinge in 2003; the review mentions Andrea Hauser's Dinge des Alltags.
Dr. Andrea Hauser's selected publications include Dinge des Alltags (1994) and Stuttgarter Frauen für den Frieden (1996).

basis: The reviewer mentions the book credited to the other key, but the review does not explicitly identify its author as the reviewer. The sources do not establish a shared institution in the relevant years or otherwise prove the identity.

evidence.says: Lisa Lieberman wrote Leaving You, studied at Yale University, and taught at Dickinson College.
Cites Lisa J. Lieberman, Une Maladie Épidémique: Suicide and its Implications in 19th Century France, Yale University, 1987.
Lisa Lieberman's 1991 article lists her affiliation as Dickinson College.

basis: The book author's Yale study and the dissertation's Yale attribution suggest a connection, but the author biography does not date her Yale study or identify the dissertation. The evidence therefore does not establish that she was at Yale in 1987.

evidence.says: Cites Andreas Osiander’s review of Daniel H. Nexon’s The Struggle for Power in Early Modern Europe.
Credits Andreas Osiander with The States System of Europe, 1640–1990 and identifies him with Humboldt-Universität, Berlin.
Credits Andreas Osiander with Before the State; the 2007 author note lists a past Humboldt University post and a current Leipzig University lectureship.

basis: The review credit and book author share a Humboldt affiliation, but the available sources do not establish that the book author held it when the review appeared in 2011 or directly link the review to either book. The evidence does not meet the brief’s test for a merge.

Susan Millar Williams wrote A Devil and a Good Woman, Too and coauthored Upheaval in Charleston; she teaches at Trident Technical College.

basis: The review gives no affiliation or other identifying detail linking its author to Susan Millar Williams. The sources found do not establish that the reviewer and the book author are the same person or different people.

evidence.says: Matthew Shannon reviewed American Culture in the 1960s for H-1960s in June 2010; the review gives no reviewer affiliation.
Matthew K. Shannon submitted Losing Hearts and Minds as a Temple University PhD dissertation in May 2013.

basis: The review does not identify an affiliation or otherwise link its author to the dissertation author. The shared name and compatible dates alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Tiffany K. Wayne lists Woman Thinking and Feminist Writings among her published works; a quoted review describes her as an independent scholar.

basis: Wayne's published-works page identifies works on key b, but does not list the 2009 review on key a. The matching name and independent-scholar description do not establish the required link between the two works.

Names Stephen George as author of The Baldrige Quality System and Uncommon Sense and describes him as a writer and consultant.

basis: The sources identify the dissertation and the business author separately, but provide no link between them or evidence that they are different people.

evidence.says: David Holm, author of Art and Ideology in Revolutionary China (1991), holds a D.Phil. in Chinese from Oxford.
David Leopold Holm earned an Oxford D.Phil. in Chinese in 1980 and was a research fellow in London in 1974–1977.
David Frederich Holm wrote The Role of the State Railways in Thai History, 1892–1932, a 1977 Yale Ph.D. dissertation.

basis: The railway dissertation is attributed to David Frederich Holm at Yale; the author of Art and Ideology was David Leopold Holm, an Oxford scholar working in London during the same period. The distinct full names and overlapping doctoral careers support two people.

evidence.says: Christopher J. Wright earned an MA in Communication, Culture, and Technology at Georgetown in 2004 and wrote Tribal Warfare.
Christopher Wright's dissertation is Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam's 'Futuhmisr': An Analysis of the Text and New Insights into the Islamic Conquest of Egypt.
Christopher Wright earned history degrees at Arkansas and a PhD in Middle East history at UC Santa Barbara; his dissertation concerns the Islamic conquest of Egypt.

basis: The 2006 book author and the dissertation author have distinct educational and professional trajectories, with work in unrelated disciplines in the same period. The institutional account of the historian's degrees does not mention the book author's 2004 Georgetown MA; this supports a difference by inference rather than an explicit disambiguation.
